clue.text: Matters abroad which involve us in strange sexual relationships

definitions.meaning: a government's dealings with other nations, handled by a foreign ministry
liaisons with partners from overseas, taking 'foreign' as strange and 'affairs' as romantic entanglements

explanation.surface: A diplomatic portfolio that drags officials into scandalous liaisons.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a ministry's international business and, read literally, amorous dalliances with outsiders.

clue.text: Do I squeal out for a concubine?

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of these three words are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Asks whether a harem woman would cry out in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DOISQUEAL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An odalisque was a female slave or mistress in an Ottoman harem, a kept companion of the sultan.

clue.text: Standing up before the court

parts.note: ere is an old word meaning before
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone rises to their feet in front of the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upright and vertical is standing tall rather than lying flat.

clue.text: Optimum achievement for bridge contractors and sportspersons

definitions.text: Optimum achievement for bridge contractors and sportspersons

parts.words: Optimum achievement for bridge contractors and sportspersons
parts.note: in bridge, bidding and making all thirteen tricks is the top contract; in tennis, golf or rugby, winning every major event in a season carries the same name

explanation.surface: Reads as praise for engineers who build bridges, alongside athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge contractors' suggests construction firms, but these are card players who bid a contract at bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means taking every trick in bridge, or sweeping all the major titles in a sport.

clue.text: More than enough drink to accommodate the member

indicators.note: to accommodate means the word for drink takes the member inside itself

parts.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer
MP, a Member of Parliament, is the usual crossword member

explanation.surface: A politician being given far too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the member' reads as a body part or club member, but in crosswords it is usually a Member of Parliament; 'to accommodate' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful supplies are generous, sufficient with something to spare.

clue.text: Original partner takes second place on board

parts.note: the original of something is the first one
a mate is a partner or companion

explanation.surface: A new partner pushes the earlier one down to runner-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second place' sounds like losing a race; on a merchant ship the officer so titled ranks second, just below the captain.
explanation.definitionFit: On a merchant vessel the chief officer serves directly under the captain, the second in command aboard.

clue.text: Cast metal at home and leave it briefly

parts.note: being in means being at home
to go is to leave

indicators.note: briefly means the word it is cut short, losing a letter

parts.note: the word it, which is then shortened

explanation.surface: Someone casts metal at home, then knocks off for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims IT to its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of gold or other metal is formed by pouring it into a mould.

clue.text: Unprofessional prospectus, unusually fishy

indicators.note: unusually tells us the remaining letters are put in an unusual order
un- read as without, and professional as its short form pro, so those letters leave the next word

explanation.surface: An amateurish brochure that strikes the reader as dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unprofessional' removes PRO from PROSPECTUS, leaving SPECTUS, which 'unusually' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishy is slang for dubious or arousing suspicion, so something that is doubtful.

clue.text: Devise complete range of cosmetics

definitions.meaning: to invent or concoct a story
the lipstick, powder and other products put on the face

explanation.surface: Dream up a full line of beauty products.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the phrase means invent; as a noun it is the cosmetics worn on the face.

clue.text: Front of Athenaeum entrance is a gem

indicators.note: front of picks out the first letter of the club's name

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: The doorway of a London club is described as a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Athenaeum is a London gentlemen's club; 'Front of' takes its first letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious stone, a kind of chalcedony.

clue.text: This vegetable is succulent because Dad rejected sweetener

parts.note: as can mean because
pa is a familiar word for dad

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for sweetener is read backwards

parts.note: sugar is a sweetener

explanation.surface: A vegetable is juicy because Father turned down sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SUGAR into RAGUS; PA stays forwards. The definition is the whole opening phrase, a vegetable described as fleshy.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a green spear-shaped shoot eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Was left holding son

indicators.note: holding means the word for left contains the letter for son

parts.note: exited means left or departed
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone departed while carrying a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts S inside EXITED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been, or to have lived, is the past sense of being.

clue.text: Allow for small space in front of name

indicators.note: in front of places the space before the name in the answer

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space, half an em
a title is a name, as of a book

explanation.surface: Leaving a short gap before a name on a form.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a right or permit is to qualify someone for something.

clue.text: Cause irritation with sound of maximum intensity

indicators.note: sound of tells us the word for maximum intensity is heard rather than written

parts.note: the peak is the point of greatest intensity

explanation.surface: Something annoys at its loudest volume.
explanation.walkthrough: PEAK and the answer are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone or wound their pride is to provoke resentment.

clue.text: Duck below the quilt

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck
down means below

explanation.surface: Telling someone to crouch beneath the bedcover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a verb meaning crouch; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedcover stuffed with soft feathers, originally from the eider, is a duvet.

clue.text: Have a good time frolicking with bird before a match

indicators.note: before places the bird ahead of the rest

parts.note: a lark is a bird
a bout is a match or contest, as in boxing

explanation.surface: Enjoying a game with a songbird before a fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To romp or fool around playfully is to have fun without seriousness.

clue.text: Organised banquet on ship out of lust

indicators.note: on places the steamship after the meal in the answer

parts.note: ran means organised or managed, as one runs a business
to banquet is to feast, to dine
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: A feast held aboard a vessel motivated by desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' looks like an anagram signal but gives RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Randiness is strong sexual desire or arousal.

clue.text: Excessively libidinous previous editor is behind the extra copies

indicators.note: behind places the previous editor after the extra copies

parts.note: overs are copies printed beyond the required number
ex means previous, a former one

explanation.surface: A former editor in a newspaper office trails the surplus print run.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing, OVERS are the surplus copies run off above the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with an abnormally strong sex drive is driven by too much desire.

clue.text: Smile and fend off the chaps who aren't batting

indicators.note: off signals that the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A cheerful way to deflect unwanted attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SMILE and FEND; 'and' merely joins. In cricket the side not batting is fielding.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the players of the bowling side spread around the ground to stop the ball.

clue.text: Emotion felt by English pair during wild spree

indicators.note: during places the two letters inside the word for spree

parts.note: a fling is a short wild spree

indicators.note: pair means the letter for English is taken twice

explanation.surface: An Englishman and partner swept up in a reckless binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felt by' is only a link joining definition and wordplay; 'pair' and 'during' are the indicators, and 'wild spree' is a single synonym, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling is an emotional state such as joy or anger.

clue.text: First lady to front National Trust do

indicators.note: to front means the first lady goes before the trust in the answer

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A president's wife leads a heritage charity's party.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the UK charity that runs historic houses. 'do' is a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is a party or social occasion, a function.

clue.text: Twice set out to fly

indicators.note: twice means the rearranged letters appear two times
out means the three letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to go out twice in order to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET to TSE, which 'Twice' repeats.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African bloodsucking insect that carries sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Type of earring requiring attention on the spot

indicators.note: on places the word for attention before the spot

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention
a drop is a spot of liquid

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery that demands notice immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the spot' reads as an idiom for immediately; it gives DROP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant hanging from the lobe is a dangling ornament.

clue.text: Adulterated pure ecstasy to make money in Asia

indicators.note: adulterated means corrupted, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Cut drugs being sold for cash somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adulterated' rearranges PURE to RUPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India, Pakistan and other South Asian countries.

clue.text: Previous leader of monks

definitions.meaning: the head of a religious house, ranking below an abbot

explanation.surface: Describes the former head of a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means earlier; as a noun it is the superior of a monastery.

clue.text: One month out-of-date represents an unsurmountable difficulty

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
passé means old-fashioned or out of date

explanation.surface: A single expired month makes for an intractable problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a situation with no way forward.

clue.text: Greek god in charge of spreading fear

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A deity in command sowing terror.
explanation.walkthrough: The word itself comes from Pan, whose sudden shouts were said to terrify.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden overwhelming alarm that sweeps through a crowd is contagious terror.

clue.text: Make do with better lives in the interior

indicators.note: in the interior means the word for lives is placed inside the word for better

parts.note: to better is to improve
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: Coping by living a better life in the heartland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' tempts as part of the definition, but it is a link; 'in the interior' signals the container, and 'lives' is the verb meaning exists.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage with whatever is at hand is to extemporise.

clue.text: Reportedly embraces American link

indicators.note: reportedly means we take the sound of the word for embraces rather than its spelling

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle, so embraces means necks
US is short for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: News that hugs are said to involve an American.
explanation.walkthrough: NECKS sounds like NEX.
explanation.definitionFit: A nexus is a connection or series of connections joining things.

clue.text: Safety guide for children puts fresh burden on conventional rules

parts.note: green means fresh or new
a cross to bear is a burden
a code is a set of conventional rules

explanation.surface: Imposing new obligations on established regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: The GREEN CROSS CODE is the British road-safety routine taught to children for crossing streets.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK guidance teaches youngsters how to cross roads without harm.
